verdict.reasoning: The rendered page 833 (A-3) matches the claim's description of the drawing: one grid, with the optional-module cells drawn beside the HIGH/INTERMEDIATE/MINIMUM rows. RPW and ITR span all three rows. Level 2 COM/DEB/SEG sit above a dividing line at mid-INTERMEDIATE, and level 1 sits below it. The markdown has the same headers and every module entry with the same level and range (1 RPW 0,1; 2/1 COM 0,2; 2/1 DEB 0,2; 2/1 SEG 0,2; 1 ITR 0,1), and it keeps level 2 above level 1. The page's own header says these modules are 'Not Required in Subsets'. So their vertical position against the subset rows carries no normative content: the mid-INTERMEDIATE split is a drawing convention that matches no subset boundary, and spanning all rows says only that the module stands outside the subsets. The claim itself concedes that every level and range is preserved and that only the drawn alignment is lost. That is a layout and formatting difference, not a change in meaning.
